note_sections.t: A urological consultation was initiated on 01 Mar 2025 after an mpMRI and a recent PSA elevation to 4.3 ng/mL.

First evaluated in 2022 for a steady PSA climb, the individual is a 76-year-old primary school teacher. Cycling to work five days a week remains part of his routine, and he cohabits with his partner despite being widowed; a longstanding friend assists with paperwork. Lower urinary tract symptoms are negligible (IPSS 1/35). Tobacco use ceased in 2014 following an 18 pack-year exposure. Recent healthcare visits include orthopaedic reviews for degenerative knee disease, dermatology appointments for actinic keratosis monitoring, and a sleep clinic evaluation for probable obstructive sleep apnoea. Invasive interventions cause considerable distress, prompting a request for detailed procedural explanations. Atorvastatin, simvastatin, and rosuvastatin manage hypercholesterolaemia, while renal parameters remain steady.

DRE — texture: firm, discrete Nodus localized to the left mid-gland peripheral zone; remaining parenchyma feels symmetrically smooth. Vitals show a blood pressure of 124/75 mmHg and a regular pulse at 67 bpm. Systemic review reveals no lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses.
